title: Tortilla de espinacas y queso feta
description: Espinacas verdes frescas, cebollas crujientes y un toque de queso feta cremoso hacen de esta tortilla una que querrás preparar una y otra vez.
ingredients: 2 tbsp queso feta bajo en grasa
steps: En un bol, sazona el sustituto de huevo con sal y pimienta y mezcla todo.
Calienta el aceite de oliva en una sartén antiadherente a fuego medio.
Agregue las cebollas rojas cortadas en cubitos y saltee hasta que se ablanden.
Añade las espinacas picadas a la sartén y cocínalas hasta que se marchiten.
Vierta los huevos sobre las espinacas y las cebollas.
A medida que los huevos comiencen a cuajar, espolvoree tomates cortados en cubitos y queso feta desmenuzado sobre la mitad de la tortilla.
Una vez que los huevos estén completamente cocidos, dobla con cuidado la tortilla por la mitad con una espátula.
Deslice la tortilla en un plato, adorne con hierbas frescas si lo desea y sirva.

title: Lechuga romana
description: Una taza de lechuga romana picada

title: Pizzas griegas con pan de pita y verduras
description: Una sabrosa mezcla de estilo Mediterráneo y pizza se unen en esta pizza griega con pan de pita y verduras. Repleta de verduras ricas en nutrientes como pimientos rojos, aceitunas, chalotas y alcachofas, esta receta rápida y fácil se prepara en menos de 15 minutos. Pruebe a servirlo con calabacín mediterráneo para una comida sustanciosa.
ingredients: 4 small pita integral (4 paneles de pita integrales de 4 pulgadas)
1 taza salsa para pizza en frasco baja en sodio (1 taza de salsa para pizza baja en sodio)
1/4 taza queso rallado italiano bajo en grasa (¼ de taza de queso rallado italiano reducido en grasas)
1/4 taza aceitunas Kalamata (¼ de taza de aceitunas kalamata en rodajas)
1/4 taza pimientos rojos asados (¼ de taza de pimientos rojos asados, cortados en rodajas finas)
1/4 taza corazones de alcachofa marinados (¼ taza de corazones de alcachofa marinados, picados)
1 chalotes (1 chalota, cortada en rodajas finas)
2 oz queso feta bajo en grasa (2 oz de queso feta reducido en grasa, desmenuzado)
1/2 taza albahaca fresca (½ taza de hojas de albahaca fresca, cortadas en juliana)
steps: Precaliente el horno a 400 grados F.
Cubra el pan de pita con salsa, aceitunas, pimientos, alcachofas, chalota y queso italiano.
Cocine en el horno hasta que el queso se derrita y la pita esté crujiente, 7-8 minutos.
Retire del horno y cubera con queso feta y albahaca fresca.

title: Sopa De Remolacha Asada Y Manzana
description: Terrosa y ligeramente dulce, me encanta preparar esta sopa en tonos escarlata a mediados o finales del otoño, cuando las manzanas y las remolachas están en su punto máximo de madurez. Es el entrante perfecto para una comida con temática otoñal, y sus contrastantes sabores dulces y ácidos complementan todo tipo de platos de temporada, desde cerdo y pollo hasta coliflor asada y coles de Bruselas.
ingredients: 1/2 lbs Remolachas rojas (recortadas y lavadas (unas 3 remolachas medianas))
2 tbsp Aceite de oliva virgen extra
1 Puerro (en rodajas (partes blancas y verde pálido))
2 Granny Smith u otra tarta de manzana (pelado, sin corazón y cortado en cubitos)
4 taza caldo de verduras bajo en sodio (Bajo en sodio)
steps: Precalienta el horno a 350°F.

Envuelva cada remolacha en un trozo de papel de aluminio y ase hasta que estén tiernas al pincharlas con un tenedor, aproximadamente 1 hora. Retira las remolachas del horno, desenvuélvelas y déjalas enfriar durante 5 minutos. Luego, quíteles la piel y corte las remolachas en dados de 1/2 pulgada.

Calienta el aceite en una cacerola mediana de fondo grueso a fuego medio-alto. Agregue el puerro y el ajo y cocine de 5 a 8 minutos o hasta que estén tiernos. Agrega las manzanas, las remolachas picadas y el jengibre. Cocine durante 1 a 2 minutos, revolviendo constantemente, luego agregue el jugo de naranja, la ralladura de naranja y el caldo.
Deje hervir el líquido, luego reduzca el fuego a bajo, cubra la cacerola y cocine a fuego lento hasta que las verduras estén muy tiernas, aproximadamente 25 minutos.

Retire la sartén del fuego, agregue el jugo de limón y deje que la sopa se enfríe un poco. Transfiera con cuidado la sopa a una licuadora o procesador de alimentos, en tandas si es necesario, y haga puré hasta que quede suave. Sazona con sal y pimienta y sirva inmediatamente.

title: Pechuga De Pavo Marroquí Asada Con Verduras De Raíz
description: Las especias marroquíes, como la canela, el cardamomo, el comino y el cilantro, son condimentos ideales para las verduras y carnes asadas. Durante el tueste, extraen la dulzura y los sabores profundos de lo que están cubriendo, y sus sabores ricos y cálidos transportan las papilas gustativas a lugares exóticos. Prepare este plato en invierno, cuando las naranjas están en temporada y la fiebre de cabaña ha comenzado a aparecer.
ingredients: 1 pechuga de pavo (con hueso, con piel)
3 tbsp Aceite de oliva virgen extra (dividido)
1 cebolla(s) (cortado por la mitad, pelado y luego cortado en cuartos)
3 costillas de apio (recortado y cortado en tercios)
2 taza zanahorias) (pelado, picado y cortado en trozos de 2 pulgadas)
2 taza nabo sueco (pelado, picado y cortado en trozos de 2 pulgadas)
1 taza nabos (pelado, picado y cortado en trozos de 2 pulgadas)
1 taza batata (pelado, picado y cortado en trozos de 2 pulgadas)
1 naranja (reducido a la mitad y luego en cuartos)
steps: Precalienta el horno a 425°F.

Afloje la piel de la pechuga de pavo empujando suavemente los dedos entre la piel y la carne. Sazone debajo de la piel con 1 cucharada de aceite de oliva, 1/2 cucharadita de sal y 1/2 cucharadita de pimienta. Frote la mezcla de especias debajo y sobre la piel suelta y luego coloque la pechuga de pavo en una fuente para asar.

En un tazón pequeño, mezcle el aceite restante, la sal y la pimienta restantes, el ajo, la cebolla, el apio, las zanahorias, el colinabo, el nabo, la batata, el orégano, la ralladura de naranja, la naranja, el comino y el pimentón ahumado. Coloca la mezcla de verduras en una sola capa alrededor de la pechuga de pavo.

Transfiera la sartén al horno y ase el pavo y las verduras, sin tapar, durante 15 minutos. Cubra la sartén sin apretar con papel de aluminio. Reduzca la temperatura del horno a 325 °F y ase durante 30 a 45 minutos más, o hasta que un termómetro de lectura instantánea insertado en la parte carnosa de la pechuga de pavo registre 165 °F.

Retire la sartén del horno, transfiera el pavo a una tabla de cortar y cúbralo sin apretar con papel de aluminio. Deje reposar el pavo durante 20 minutos, luego deseche la piel y corte la carne en rodajas.
Retire y deseche las naranjas de las verduras asadas, revuelva bien las verduras y sírvalas con el pavo en rodajas.

title: Barras de mantequilla de maní y chispas de chocolate
description: Aumenté esta versión de una "rubia" con la ventaja de la bondad de la mantequilla de maní. ¡Estas barras son un gran ejemplo de un postre que es lo suficientemente dulce, pero ridículamente satisfactorio!
ingredients: 1/3 taza jarabe de arce puro (preferiblemente grado B)
1/4 taza leche de almendras sin azúcar
1/2 taza mantequilla de maní sin azúcar agregada
3/4 taza harina de garbanzos o harina de espelta
1/3 taza chispas de chocolate amargo endulzadas con stevia (sin azúcares añadidos)
steps: Precalienta el horno a 350°F. Cubra una fuente para hornear de 9 x 9 pulgadas con aceite en aerosol antiadherente.

En el bol de una batidora eléctrica, o con una batidora de mano, bata el huevo, la clara de huevo, el aceite, el jarabe de arce, el plátano, la leche de almendras, la vainilla y la mantequilla de maní hasta que quede suave. Deje los ingredientes húmedos a un lado.
En un tazón grande aparte, mezcle la harina de almendras, la harina de garbanzos, la linaza, el polvo para hornear y el bicarbonato de sodio.

Agrega los ingredientes secos a los ingredientes húmedos y revuelve con una cuchara de madera o una espátula hasta que estén bien combinados. Incorpora las chispas de chocolate. Vierta la masa en la fuente para hornear preparada y extiéndala uniformemente.
Transfiera el molde al horno y hornee por 30 minutos, o hasta que al introducir un palillo en el centro, éste salga limpio.
Retire el molde del horno, déjelo enfriar un poco y luego córtelo en 16 barras.

title: Pollo Frito Al Horno
description: Este pollo “frito” no solo es más saludable que el pollo frito tradicional, sino que también es más fácil y menos complicado de preparar que la versión tradicional.
ingredients: 2 taza Pan rallado integral estilo italiano
2 large huevos (batido con 1 cucharada de agua)
8 muslos de pollo (deshuesado, sin piel, alrededor de 2 libras)
steps: Precaliente el horno a 375°F de convección o a 400°F en el horno tradicional. Coloque el pan rallado, el ajo y la mezcla de condimentos italianos para cocinar sin estrés en el procesador de alimentos. Procese hasta que esté bien mezclado.
Coloque la harina en un molde para pastel. Coloque los huevos y las claras en un molde para pastel aparte. Coloque la mezcla de pan rallado en un tercer molde para pastel.
Forre una bandeja para hornear grande con papel pergamino.

Sumerja el pollo en harina y cúbralo por todos lados, luego en huevo y luego en pan rallado. Cubra uniformemente. Colóquelo en una bandeja para hornear forrada con papel pergamino. Si tienes tiempo, refrigera el pollo un rato antes de cocinarlo.

Hornee el pollo durante 45 minutos hasta que esté crujiente y bien dorado. Sirva con condimentos para picnic o ensaladas. Se puede preparar con anticipación y congelar para recalentar en un horno muy caliente. Descongelar antes de recalentar.

title: Salmón balsámico sobre pilaf de cebada
ingredients: 1 lbs salmón (sin piel, cortado en 4 trozos (4 oz cada uno))
1/2 taza albahaca fresca (picado en trozos grandes)
1 pints tomates cherry (Cortar por la mitad)
3 taza caldo de pollo bajo en sodio
steps: Coloque el aceite de canola en una olla grande. Calienta y agrega la cebolla, el ajo y el apio. Cocine a fuego medio, tapado, hasta que la cebolla se vuelva transparente. Agregue las zanahorias y la cebada y cocine sin tapar hasta que la cebada comience a verse tostada. Añadir caldo. Tapar y cocinar 30 minutos.

Corte los tomates por la mitad y colóquelos en un tazón grande con vinagre balsámico, albahaca, sal, pimienta y salmón. Déjelo reposar mientras se cocina la cebada durante los primeros 30 minutos. Después de 30 minutos, retira el salmón de la mezcla de tomate. Agrega la mezcla de tomate a la cebada y coloca el salmón encima de la cebada. Tape y cocine 10 minutos más para cocinar el salmón al vapor.
Coloque un poco de pilaf de cebada en un tazón de pasta y cubra con un trozo de salmón para servir.

title: Pepinos agridulces
description: Esta receta presentada por DaVita, un orgulloso socio de la American Diabetes Association® y Diabetes Food Hub®
steps: El líquido de marinado se debe escurrir bien y desechar de los pepinos antes de servir. Sirva en ensaladeras pequeñas como ensalada o refrigerio.
Cubra el recipiente con papel film y déjelo en el refrigerador durante las últimas 2 horas.
Vierta sobre los pepinos y la cebolla. Agregue pimienta y, si lo desea, ¼ de cucharadita de sal.
Combine el azúcar y el vinagre. Mezclar hasta que el azúcar se disuelva por completo.
Corte los pepinos y las cebollas en rodajas de aproximadamente 1/8 de pulgada de grosor. Colóquelo en un tazón grande.

title: Tofu glaseado con sésamo y arce con quinua vegetal y furikake
description:
Para este plato vibrante, dorarás tofu y lo glasearás en la sartén con una mezcla dulce y salada de aceite de sésamo, jarabe de arce y más, luego lo servirás sobre una abundante cama de quinua mezclada con repollo salteado, zanahorias, y setas.

Blue Apron cree que la hora de comer debería ser la mejor parte del día. Es por eso que colaboramos con la Asociación Estadounidense de Diabetes para servir comidas deliciosas, listas para cocinar, repletas de productos frescos, proteínas magras y muchas opciones sabrosas. Todo enviado a tu puerta.
ingredients: 2 tbsp aminoácidos de coco o salsa de soja baja en sodio
steps: Cocina la quinua: Llena una olla mediana hasta 3/4 de su capacidad con agua con sal; cubra y caliente hasta que hierva a temperatura alta. Una vez que hierva, agregue la quinua y cocine, sin tapar, de 18 a 20 minutos o hasta que esté tierna. Apaga el fuego. Escurrir bien y volver a la olla.

Presione el tofu: Mientras tanto, escurra el tofu y luego colóquelo en un plato forrado con papel toalla. Coloque varias capas de toallas de papel encima y luego coloque una olla (o sartén) de fondo grueso encima de las toallas de papel. Reservar para que suelte el exceso de líquido al menos 10 minutos.

Prepare los ingredientes y haga el glaseado: Mientras tanto, lave y seque los productos frescos. Pelar las zanahorias; cortar en rodajas finas en ángulo. Corta los champiñones en trozos pequeños. Corta y desecha el corazón del repollo; Cortar finamente las hojas. Pelar y picar finamente el jengibre. Pelar y picar en trozos grandes 2 dientes de ajo. Cortar las cebolletas en rodajas finas, separando la parte inferior blanca y la parte superior verde hueca. En un tazón, combine el repollo en rodajas, el jengibre picado, el ajo picado y las partes blancas de las cebolletas en rodajas. En un recipiente aparte, mezcle los aminoácidos de coco, el jarabe de arce, la mitad del aceite de sésamo y 1 cucharada de agua.

Cocine las verduras y termine la quinua: en una sartén mediana (antiadherente, si tiene una), caliente el aceite de sésamo restante a fuego medio-alto hasta que esté caliente. Agregue las zanahorias en rodajas y los trozos de champiñones en una capa uniforme. Cocine, sin revolver, de 2 a 3 minutos o hasta que esté ligeramente dorado. Agrega la mezcla de repollo preparada; sazone con sal (opcional) y pimienta. Cocine, revolviendo ocasionalmente, de 2 a 3 minutos, o hasta que se ablanden. Agrega el vinagre. Cocine, revolviendo con frecuencia, de 30 segundos a 1 minuto, o hasta que el líquido se haya evaporado. Transfiera a la olla de quinua cocida; revuelve para combinar. Cubrir para mantener el calor. Enjuague y limpie la sartén.

Cocine el tofu y sirva su plato: Transfiera el tofu prensado a una tabla de cortar; córtelo a lo largo en 4 trozos del mismo tamaño. Sazone con sal (opcional) y pimienta por ambos lados. En la misma sartén, calienta 2 cucharaditas de aceite de oliva a fuego medio-alto hasta que esté caliente. Agregue los trozos de tofu sazonados en una capa uniforme y cocine de 5 a 6 minutos, o hasta que se doren. Voltee y cocine de 2 a 3 minutos, o hasta que esté ligeramente dorado. Agregue la mitad del glaseado (con cuidado, ya que el líquido puede salpicar) y cocine, vertiendo frecuentemente el glaseado sobre el tofu, de 1 a 2 minutos, o hasta que el tofu esté cubierto. Transfiera a una tabla de cortar. Córtelo transversalmente en trozos de 1 pulgada. Sirva la quinua terminada cubierta con el tofu cocido y el glaseado restante. Adorne con las puntas verdes en rodajas de las cebolletas y el furikake. ¡Disfrutar!

title: Frutas a la Plancha con Crema de Yogurt de Vainilla
description: Asar a la parrilla carameliza los azúcares naturales de las frutas, dándoles un sabor más rico y dulce que sabe más a postre que a un refrigerio saludable. Estamos usando una combinación de melocotones, ciruelas y albaricoques, pero 6 frutas de hueso veraniegas cualesquiera servirán. Para darle aún más sabor, cubrimos la fruta con yogur bajo en grasa y un ligero chorrito de miel. Para que quede más crujiente, intente cubrir con nueces picadas; los pistachos funcionan particularmente bien. Esta receta apareció en:
ingredients: 2 melocotones maduros (cortado por la mitad, sin huesos)
2 ciruelas maduras (cortado por la mitad, sin huesos)
2 damascos maduros (cortado por la mitad, sin huesos)
1 taza yogur de vainilla bajo en grasa
steps: Coloque los duraznos, las ciruelas y los albaricoques en la parrilla, con el lado cortado hacia abajo. Ase a fuego lento o indirecto hasta que estén suaves, aproximadamente de 2 a 4 minutos por cada lado.
Coloque la fruta en una fuente para servir y cubra uniformemente con yogur, linaza molida y almendras molidas.
Rocíe miel sobre cada porción y decore con una pizca de canela. Si lo desea, espolvoree pistachos picados sobre cada uno. Servir inmediatamente.

title: Pizza de Pesto de Durazno
description: Esta receta sencilla combina tres de nuestras P favoritas: pesto, peach (durazno) y pizza. Si adoras lo dulce y sabroso y estás buscando una receta de pizza creativa sin gluten y con una corteza de coliflor para mezclarla en casa, no busques más. Esta receta traída a ti por CAULIPOWERÂ®, un orgulloso promotor de la American Diabetes AssociationÂ® y del Diabetes Food HubÂ®.
ingredients: 1 whole masa de pizza de coliflor
steps: Precalienta el horno a 425°F (218°C).
Retira tu corteza de pizza CAULIPOWER® de la caja y del envoltorio plástico, y colócala sobre una superficie limpia.
Esparce la salsa de pesto uniformemente sobre la corteza de pizza CAULIPOWER®.
Cubre con durazno, hinojo, cebolla morada, y parmesano y hornea de 13 a 16 minutos.
Retírala del horno y agrega rúgula y almendras fileteadas, y rocía un glaseado balsámico sobre la pizza.

title: Berenjena griega asada con queso feta
ingredients: 2 berenjena (cada uno cortado en cuartos a lo largo en gajos, sin tallos)
1 limón (rallado y en jugo, uso dividido)
steps: Precalienta el horno a 400° F. En un tazón pequeño, mezcla la salsa marinara, el jugo de limón, el aceite, el ajo y la canela. Coloque las rodajas de berenjena, con la piel hacia abajo, en una bandeja para hornear forrada con papel pergamino sin blanquear. Unte generosamente la pulpa de las rodajas de berenjena con la mezcla de marinara.
Ase las rodajas de berenjena hasta que estén bien cocidas y suaves, aproximadamente 30 minutos.
Transfiera las rodajas a un plato. Espolvorea con perejil, menta, queso feta y ralladura de limón y sirve.

title: Pasta cremosa con pollo y albahaca
description: ¿Le apetece un reconfortante plato de pasta? Pruebe haciendo esta pasta cremosa con pollo y albahaca apta para diabéticos. La salsa casera a base de hierbas frescas añade una explosión de sabor que hará de esta receta una de las favoritas de la familia.
ingredients: 1/4 taza albahaca fresca (¼ de taza de hojas de albahaca fresca, cortadas en juliana)
1/4 taza queso parmesano (¼ de taza de queso parmesano recién rallado)
2 taza pasta penne integral (2 tazas de pasta integral cocida)
1 lbs pechugas de pollo deshuesadas y sin piel (1 libra de pechugas de pollo deshuesadas y sin piel, cortadas por la mitad longitudinalmente en filetes finos)
1/2 tsp condimento italiano sin sal añadida (½ cucharadita de condimento italiano bajo en sodio o sin sal añadida)
1/2 taza queso italiano bajo en grasa (½ taza de queso italiano)
3 taza leche sin grasa (3 tazas de leche descremada)
1/2 tsp cebolla en polvo (½ cucharadita de cebolla en polvo)
1 tsp ajo (1 cucharadita de ajo picado)
3 tbsp aceite de oliva (3 cucharadas de aceite de oliva, separado)
2 tbsp mitad y mitad (2 cucharadas de mitad y mitad)
1/2 taza perejil fresco (½ taza de perejil italiano de hoja plana envasado)
1 taza albahaca fresca (1 taza de hojas de albahaca envasadas)
5 oz espinacas tiernas (5 oz de espinacas tiernas)
steps: Ponga una olla grande de agua a hervir. Añada las espinacas tiernas a la olla y escáldelas durante 1 minuto. Utilice una espumadera para retirar las espinacas y colocarlas en un bol con agua helada. Agregue el perejil y la albahaca envasada a la olla y escalde durante 15 segundos. Retire y añada al bol de agua helada. Escurra el agua y exprime todo el líquido posible de las verduras.
Añada las espinacas, el perejil y la albahaca a un procesador de alimentos. Añada la mitad y la mitad al procesador de alimentos y haga un puré. Reservar.

Caliente una cacerola a fuego medio. Añada 2 cucharadas de aceite de oliva, ajo y cebolla en polvo. Agrega la harina y bata durante 1 minuto. Añada la leche y batir hasta obtener una mezcla homogénea.
Añada el queso, el condimento italiano, la sal (opcional) y la pimienta. Revuelva hasta que la salsa especial.
Añada el puré de verduras y revuelva para mezclar.
Mientras tanto, caliente una sartén grande a fuego medio. Añada el aceite de oliva restante. Cocine el pollo durante 3-4 minutos por cada lado, hasta que esté dorado y bien cocido.
Para servir, reparta el pollo y la pasta en los platos. Cubra con salsa, queso parmesano y albahaca fresca en juliana.

title: Panqueques de harina de almendras sin gluten
description: Disfruta de tu mañana con estos panqueques de harina de almendras sin gluten que aportan suficiente proteína para mantenerte con energía. Si tu plan de alimentación para el control de la diabetes lo permite, añádele rodajas de banana fresca o frutos rojos bajos en carbohidratos.
ingredients: 1/2 taza leche de almendras sin azúcar
steps: En un bol, mezcle la harina de almendras, la harina de coco, el polvo para hornear y la sal.
En un recipiente aparte, bate los huevos y añade la leche de almendras, 1 cucharada de aceite de oliva, el jarabe de arce y el extracto de vainilla. Mezcla bien.
Vierta los ingredientes húmedos en los ingredientes secos y revuelva hasta que se integren. Deje reposar la masa durante un par de minutos para que espese.
Calienta una sartén o plancha a fuego medio y engrasa con 1 cucharadita de aceite de oliva o aceite en aerosol.
Vierta ¼ de taza de masa en la sartén para cada panqueque. Extienda la masa ligeramente con el dorso de una cuchara.
Cocine hasta que se formen burbujas en la superficie, luego voltee y cocine hasta que el otro lado esté dorado.
Repita con la masa restante.

title: Wrap de pollo y lechuga tierna
description: ¡LECHUGA te presenta tu nuevo wrap de pollo más saludable y favorito! Elaborada con filetes de pollo HORNO (nunca fritos) de CAULIPOWER, esta sabrosa receta no contiene gluten, lácteos y está repleta de proteínas, ¡lo que hace que su almuerzo entre semana sea un poco más CAULIPOWERful! Esta receta presentada por CAULIPOWER®, un orgulloso partidario de la American Diabetes Association® y Diabetes Food Hub®.
ingredients: 2 Tiras de pollo originales CAULIPOWER® (ofertas, 85 g)
steps: Precaliente el horno a 425 grados F.
Coloque los filetes de pollo CAULIPOWER en una bandeja para hornear que haya sido rociada con aceite en aerosol antiadherente.
Caliente de 17 a 19 minutos para el horno convencional, de 15 a 17 minutos para el horno de convección o hasta que los tiernos alcancen una temperatura interna de 165 grados F.
Retire los filetes del horno y coloque los filetes calientes sobre la lechuga.
Cubra con zanahorias, cebollas verdes, aguacate, col lombarda y pico de gallo.

title: Spicy duck topped poppadoms
description: These look impressive but are actually very simple to make. Mini poppadoms are ideal for a drinks party.
ingredients: 2 duck breasts, skin and fat removed (weight 400g)
6cm piece cucumber, seeds removed finely chopped
steps: Place the duck breasts in a non-metallic dish and rub all over with the Chinese 5 spice powder. Leave to marinate for at least 10 minutes. Slice the duck into small pieces.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan. Add the duck and fry for 2-3 minutes until crisp and golden.
Mix together the cucumber, coriander and spring onions and place a little onto each poppadom.
Spoon on a little mango chutney and top each poppadom with a piece of duck.
hints: You could use chicken breast or lean steak in place of duck.
For a vegan version, replace the duck with small cubes of tofu.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 0

title: Crisp salmon salad
description: Potatoes, tomatoes and salmon combine to make this hearty salad.
steps: Boil the potatoes for 10–15 minutes until tender then refresh in cold water, cool a little and slice.
Toss together the potato slices and tomatoes and divide between 2 serving dishes. Pile the salad leaves on top and set aside.
Coat one side of each salmon fillet with pepper.
Heat a non-stick frying pan or a griddle until hot. Place the salmon pepper-side down and cook for 3–4 minutes, then turn and cook a further 3–4 minutes until thoroughly cooked through.
Lay the salmon on top of the salad leaves, mix together the orange rind and juice with the mustard, drizzle over the salad and serve.
hints: This salad works well with other fish, such as mackerel fillets, fresh tuna or with king prawns. You could also use thinly sliced chicken breast.
For a vegan alternative try strips of tofu instead of salmon. Simply fry in a non-stick pan until crisp then toss with a little sesame oil, soy sauce and Chinese five spice.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 1

title: Potato pizza
description: An alternative vegetarian pizza topping to regular cheese and tomato.
steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C/gas 7.
Place the flours and yeast in a large bowl. Mix together the milk, oil and 125ml warm water, pour over the flour and bring together to form a soft dough.
Tip onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 5-6 minutes until smooth. Place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth and set aside in a warm place for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, simmer the potatoes in lightly salted water for 5 minutes. Drain.
Heat the oil in a non-stick frying pan and fry the onion for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Cut the dough in two and shape each piece into a 23cm circle, approximately ½-1cm thick, and place on a heavy baking sheet.
Prepare the topping, adding the rosemary, thyme, creme fraiche and pepper to the potatoes and divide between the bases. Set aside for 5 minutes, then bake for 15-20 minutes until crisp and golden.
hints: Scatter the cooked pizza with a handful of fresh rocket leaves and a dash of balsamic vinegar or a few chopped cherry tomatoes and a couple of chopped spring onions.
Try spreading 1 tsp curry paste over the pizza base before cooking.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 0

title: Vietnamese beef salad
description: A filling but light salad with tender beef and beansprouts.
steps: Add the oil to a pan. Add the beef and cook for 4–5 minutes over a high heat, stirring regularly. Stir in the chilli flakes, garlic and ginger.
Next, add the red pepper, stirring for 2–3 minutes, followed by the baby sweetcorn. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the beansprouts and spring onions, mix well for 1 minute and remove from the heat. Allow to cool.
For the dressing, add the cucumber, coriander, lime juice and soy sauce to a small bowl.
Add the dressing to the noodles and mix in well. Next, add the cooled beef mixture, mix together and serve.
hints: Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 1

title: Chicken balti
description: A fragrant, flavoursome and warming balti dish.
steps: Add the oil to a pan, followed by the onion, and cook for 3–4 minutes until softened. Add the chicken and cook for 2–3 minutes.
Add the pepper, carrot and celery, and cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring regularly.
Add the garlic, curry powder and garam masala, and stir well to coat everything in the spices.
Add the chilli, tomatoes and tomato purée, and bring to a gentle boil.
Cover and simmer for 12–14 minutes until the carrot is tender. Mix in the coriander and serve.
hints: We’ve used curry powder – unlike curry paste, it doesn’t have added salt or fat.
You could use lean pork or cubes of lamb for this dish. For a vegetarian/vegan version, replace the chicken with a tin of chickpeas or mixed beans.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 3

title: Asparagus frittata
description: A super tasty lunch with only four ingredients required.
ingredients: ½ medium bag (e.g 150g) fresh spinach leaves
1 Cal Spray Oil (approximately 7 sprays of oil)
steps: Snap the ends off the asparagus where they naturally break then cut into large-ish chunks.
Finely chop the spring onion.
Beat the eggs together then season with black pepper to taste.
Spray a small frying pan with 1cal oil and place over a medium heat.
Fry the spring onion, and asparagus for a few minutes, until starting to soften.
Add spinach and cook a further few minutes until spinach has wilted.
Pour the beaten eggs into the pan, spread the asparagus evenly through the mixture and cook for around 5 mins, until the edges are starting to brown.
Remove the pan from the hob and place under a hot grill until the frittata starts to brown.
hints: Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 2

title: Carrot cake
description: This healthier version is easy to make. We cut it into 18 but you could easily divide it into 24 small squares for a party.
ingredients: 50ml rapeseed oil + 2 tsp to oil the tin
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C/gas 4 and lightly grease a 20cm x 25cm cm cake tin with the rapeseed oil.
In a bowl, mix the flour, baking powder and spice together.
In another bowl add egg and banana and beat well. Mix in the sweetener and oil.
Gradually fold the dry ingredients into the banana, egg and oil mixture, then fold in the sultanas and carrots.
Pile the mixture into cake tin and bake for 25-30 minutes then remove from the oven and allow to cool on a wire rack.
When the cake is cool, cover with the sweetened quark and top with orange zest and walnut pieces.
hints: Make sure the cake is completely cooled before topping otherwise the cream cheese will melt.
Try cutting into small squares before you top it, then pipe a blob of sweetened cream cheese onto each square and sprinkle with orange zest and a piece of walnut.
You could use cinnamon in place of mixed spice or try using different nuts such as hazelnuts or almonds.

title: Butternut squash and borlotti bean stew
description: A colourful winter dish you can cook in one pan.
ingredients: 1 medium butternut squash, deseeded, peeled and cubed
1 vegetable stock cube dissolved in 500ml water
steps: Heat the oil in a pan and add the onions, squash and green pepper. Stir regularly for 5 minutes until starting to brown.
Add the stock, tomatoes, red lentils, oregano, chilli and garlic. Bring to the boil, reduce the heat, add a lid and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the beans and heat for a further 10 minutes, check the squash is cooked through (until tender). Serve with a good grind of black pepper and a sprinkle of parsley.
hints: Ideal with pumpkin instead of the butternut squash.
Any beans work well, you could use two different types or cans of mixed beans.
Try stuffing into halved peppers, top with a sprinkle of cheese and bake in the oven 180°/gas 4 for 15 minutes until the pepper is soft and the cheese browned.
Freezing instructions: Suitable for freezing once cooked. Then defrost in the fridge and reheat in the mircowave or on a hob until piping hot throughout.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 5

title: Apple and cinnamon cake
description: A tasty dessert made with wholemeal flour
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C/gas 6.
Sift the flour into a bowl, add the artifical sweetener, baking powder and cinnamon into the flour and mix.
Make a well in the middle of the dry ingredients and add the eggs and the milk. Whisk and add in the melted butter.
Peel and core the apples and remove the seeds. Cut them into large slices. Add the apple slices to the mixture and fold in gently.
Grease a cake tin (around 23cm in diameter) with some vegetable oil. Pour the mixture into the tin and bake in the oven for 35 minutes.
Turn out onto a cooling rack. Leave to cool and serve.
hints: Start by preparing the batter, in order to leave it aside while you peel the apples.
You can also replace the apples with pears, and the cinnamon with ground ginger or mixed spice.

title: Roasted cauliflower, paneer and chickpea curry
description: A deliciously tasty vegetable curry with paneer and chickpeas. Topped with spicy, crispy roasted cauliflower.
ingredients: 1 low-salt vegetable stock cube, dissolved in 400ml water
steps: Preheat the oven 180°C/gas mark 4 and lightly oil a baking sheet with 1 tsp of oil.

Rinse the cauliflower in cold water, shake off any excess, then add to a bowl. Sprinkle with turmeric and mix well. Place on the baking sheet and roast for 20 minutes, until the edges are starting to char, then set aside.
Meanwhile, add 1 tsp oil to a pan and add the onion. Cook for 3-4 minutes until softened, but not browned.
Add the sweet potato, red pepper, garlic, cumin and curry paste, then cook for a further 2-3 minutes, stirring regularly.
Pour over the stock, mix well, cover, then simmer for 8-10 minutes until the potato is almost tender.
Add the paneer, chickpeas and peas, then continue to boil without the lid for 5-6 minutes. Stir in the yogurt and serve topped with the roasted cauliflower.
hints: Experiment with mixed beans or cannellini beans rather than chickpeas.
Try adding different vegetables such as 150g fresh spinach or mushrooms.
You can use a plain yoghurt of your choice, but this will change the nutritional information.
Freezing instructions: Suitable for freezing once cooked. Defrost in the fridge or microwave, then reheat until piping hot throughout.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 4

title: Moroccan-style chicken
description: Serve this dish with couscous for a real North African treat.
ingredients: 2 tbsp fresh mint chopped, plus extra to garnish
steps: Wrap each chicken thigh around a cinnamon stick.
Mix together the garlic, paprika, cumin and half the oil. Place the chicken into a non-metallic dish, spoon over the spice mixture and coat, then leave to marinate for at least 1 hour.
Heat the remaining oil in a pan, add the chicken pieces (still wrapped around the cinnamon stick) and brown all over. Remove from the pan using a slotted spoon and set aside.
Add the carrot and beans to the pan, cook over a low heat for about 5–6 minutes. Stir in the turmeric and add all the remaining ingredients to the pan, along with the chicken.
Pour over the stock, bring to the boil cover and simmer for 12–15 minutes, until the chicken is tender.
Season, garnish with mint and serve with plenty of steamed couscous.
hints: If you don’t have cinnamon sticks add 1 tsp ground cinnamon to the marinade.
For a gluten-free alternative, serve with basmati rice sprinkled with pomegranate seeds.
Freezing instructions: Suitable for freezing once cooked. Then defrost in the fridge or microwave and reheat until piping hot throughout.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 1

title: Jerk chicken with chargrilled pineapple salsa
description: A classic Jamaican dish that’s popular across the Caribbean. Jerk refers to the spicy seasoning the chicken is marinated in. Can be cooked in the oven or on the barbecue.
ingredients: 4 spring onions, trimmed and finely chopped
1 red chilli, deseeded and finely chopped
1 lime, finely grated, zested and juiced
1 medium-sized fresh pineapple, rind removed, or 8 rings of canned pineapple
1 green chilli, deseeded and finely chopped
½ small red onion, finely chopped
Small handful fresh coriander, finely chopped
For the carrot and apple slaw
For the carrot and apple slaw
1 Granny Smith apple, cored and coarsely grated
For the carrot and apple slaw
For the carrot and apple slaw
steps: Using a sharp knife, slash the chicken flesh a few times and place in a non-metallic dish. Dry fry the allspice berries for 2–3 minutes until fragrant, then tip into a mortar and pound to a powder. Add the remaining jerk ingredients and pound to a thick paste. Stir into the chicken to coat evenly. Cover and leave to marinate overnight if you have time, or for at least 1 hour.

Meanwhile, cut out and discard the core of the pineapple and slice the flesh. Heat a chargrill pan until smoking. Spray the pineapple with low-calorie cooking spray and chargrill for 2 mins on each side until pleasantly charred with lines.

Preheat the grill to high. Place the chicken on a grill rack over a baking tray and grill for 20–25 minutes, turning occasionally until cooked through (check with a meat thermometer or by pushing a metal skewer into the thickest part of the chicken – if the juices run clear it is cooked. If not, pop back under the grill for 4–5 mins, then test again).

While the chicken is cooking, toss together the carrots, apples and cider vinegar. Season with freshly ground black pepper and sprinkle over the seeds. Serve with the chicken and salsa. Scatter a little extra coriander and red chilli over the chicken if desired.
hints: This recipe is high in protein and vitamin C and is a source of iron.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 2

title: Fillet of lamb with minted couscous
description: This mouthwatering recipe combining fresh, chopped mint is an ideal dish for entertaining.
ingredients: 400ml vegetable stock (use gluten-free vegetable stock to make this recipe gluten-free)
175g couscous (use quinoa to make this recipe gluten-free)
steps: Place the lamb on a baking tray and season with black pepper.
Heat the redcurrant jelly and pour over the lamb. Use a pastry bush to spread the jelly all over.
Cook the lamb under a hot grill for 10-15 minutes. Remove from the grill, cover with foil and allow to rest for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, bring the vegetable stock to the boil and add the spices. Add the couscous, remove from the heat and cover with a lid. Leave to steam for 1 minute then fluff up the grains with a fork.
Stir in the chopped mint tomatoes, parsley, lemon juice and zest and pile onto serving plates.
Carve the lamb into thin slices and arrange on top of the couscous.
hints: You could also use chicken breast or pork fillet with this recipe.
Freezing instructions: Freeze couscous and lamb separately. Defrost in the fridge or microwave and reheat until piping hot throughout.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 1

title: Mulligatawny soup
description: Perfect for cold evenings, this warming, spicy soup is packed with vegetables, lentils and rice.
ingredients: 75g basmati rice cooked in 1 litre boiling water
steps: Add the oil to a large pan with the onion. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring regularly, until it starts to brown.
Add the carrot and sweet potato, and cook for a further 5 minutes, stirring regularly.
Now add the tomatoes, lentils, garlic, stock cube, curry paste and 1 litre of boiling water. Bring to the boil, turn down the heat, cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil the rice for 10 minutes, rinse in a sieve under cold water and reserve.
Blend the vegetables with a stick blender or food processor until smooth.
Stir the rice into the soup and serve with a sprinkle of freshly chopped coriander.
hints: Add a finely diced chicken breast along with the tomatoes and use a chicken stock cube.
This recipe is high in Vitamin A, which helps to keep your immune system working properly.
Freezing instructions: Suitable for freezing once cooked. Freeze in portions then defrost in the fridge, or defrost in a microwave stirring regularly.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 1

title: Welsh Leek Rarebit
description: A simple, healthier version of cheese on toast. Perfect for breakfast or brunch.
steps: Add the oil to a pan, then add the chopped leek and cook over a low to medium heat, stirring frequently, for 4 minutes until it is soft.
Remove the leek from the heat and allow it to cool for a few minutes.
Meanwhile, turn on the grill to high and toast one side of the rye bread.
Add the egg to a bowl with the mustard, and beat lightly. Next, stir in half the grated cheese and all the leek.
Spread the mixture evenly over the untoasted side of the bread, sprinkle with the remaining cheese and grill for about 2–3 minutes until golden brown.
hints: Using a mature Cheddar means you can use less and still get a strong flavour.
Rye bread is an excellent wholegrain – it’s high in fibre and will keep you feeling fuller for longer, so is ideal for breakfast.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 1

title: Open sardine sandwich with chilli
description: A tasty and filling lunch you can make in under 5 minutes.
ingredients: 120g tin of sardines in olive oil
steps: Deseed and finely slice ½ small red chilli.
Drain a can of sardines, reserving some of the oil.
Put a handful of rocket on top of the slices of bread and arrange the sardines on top.
Scatter with the chilli slices and drizzle over a little of the reserved oil.
hints: Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 0

title: Smoked salmon and chive mini tartlets
description: Mouthwatering seafood morsels, great for serving with drinks.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200ºC/gas 6.
Roll out the pastry thinly. Stamp out about 36 x 5cm rounds with a pastry cutter and use to line mini tartlet tins. Bake blind for 10 minutes.
Beat together the egg and crème fraiche, season well then stir through the chives and salmon.
Spoon a little mixture into each of the pastry cases and cook for about 10 minutes, until golden and set.
Allow to cool a little and serve.
hints: You could use smoked ham in place of salmon.
For a veggie version, use sliced sundried tomatoes to replace the smoked salmon.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 0

title: Vegetable moussaka
description: A hearty but lower-fat dish packed with vegetables and higher in fibre, topped with cheesy-spiced yogurt.
ingredients: 1 sweet potato (approx. 350g), peeled and cut into 0.5cm-thick slices
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C/gas 4. Boil the sweet potato slices for 7-10 minutes until just tender. Drain and set aside.
Grill the aubergine slices for 4 minutes on each side and set aside.
Add the oil to a pan and add the onions. When they start to brown, add the peppers, courgettes and carrots. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, lentils, tomatoes, oregano and thyme. Bring to the boil, turn down the heat, cover and simmer for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, to make the topping mix the yogurt, Cheddar and cinnamon together.

In an ovenproof dish, place a layer of aubergine, add a spoonful of the lentil and tomato mixture, followed by a layer of sweet potato. Top with more of the lentil and tomato mixture, and layer alternately, finishing with the aubergine.
Spoon the yogurt mixture over the top and bake for 15 minutes.
hints: You could make individual moussaka in ovenproof dishes to serve direct to the table.
For the best flavour, allow to stand for 5-10 minutes before serving.
Freezing instructions: Suitable for freezing once cooked. Defrost in the fridge or microwave and reheat thoroughly until piping-hot throughout.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 3

title: Mini Christmas puddings
description: Bite-sized, healthier version of the traditional Christmas pudding. No added sugar and oatmeal, mashed banana and apple instead of traditional suet (animal fat).
steps: Preheat the oven to 170°C/ gas 3. Put the mixed fruit, figs and spices into a bowl. Mix, then add the boiling water, cover and leave to stand for 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, mash the banana and mix in the grated apple, oatmeal, ground almonds, seeds and zest.
Next, combine everything together in one bowl, mixing well.
Lightly oil two 12-cup mini bun tins (or simply make 2 batches in the same tin) and place the mixture into the tins.
Bake in the oven for 15-25 minutes, depending on the size of the bun tins.
When cooked (they are firm and a knife comes out clean), turn out onto a wire rack and allow to cool.
hints: You can use any sized bun tin, just adjust the cooking time accordingly, as larger buns will take longer to cook.
These small puddings cook much more quickly and you don't need to steam them, making them ideal for pre-Christmas parties, too.
Try topping with nuts or orange slices for super-luxury puddings.
Freezing instructions: Defrost in the microwave then steam, microwave, or heat in a moderate oven.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 0

title: Spicy potato wedges
description: Great for entertaining and delightfully healthy – much lower in fat than shop-bought versions. Please note: dips are not included in the analysis.
ingredients: 8 baking potatoes, each cut into 8 wedges (total weight 1.6kg)
For the garlic and herb dip
For the garlic and herb dip
For the garlic and herb dip
For the garlic and herb dip
For the garlic and herb dip
steps: Preheat the oven to 200ºC/gas 6.
Place the potato wedges in a large pan of boiling water and simmer for 5 minutes. Drain and place in a large roasting tin.
Mix together the oil and the paprika and toss through the potato wedges. Place on a baking tray and cook for 20-25 minutes until golden and crisp.
For the garlic and herb dip, simply combine all the ingredients and spoon into a serving dish.
Drain any excess liquid from the tomatoes then blend with the chilli, garlic and coriander for 30 seconds. Spoon into a serving dish.
Serve the potatoes with the dips.
hints: If you’re passing these around as finger food, omit the paprika from the potatoes as it stains the fingers!
You could use Chinese 5 Spice powder in place of paprika, or try dried thyme.
Freezing instructions: Wedges are suitable for freezing. Defrost in the microwave and reheat in the oven until piping hot.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 0

title: Wholemeal spinach and cheddar pancakes
description: Chunky, cheesy pancakes topped with tomatoes and basil.
ingredients: 200g frozen spinach, defrosted, excess water removed
50g reduced-fat mature cheddar cheese, finely diced
steps: Add 1 tsp of oil to a saucepan over a low to medium heat, then add the onion. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring regularly until softened, then remove from the heat.
Beat the egg into the milk, then place the flour in a bowl and gradually stir in the milk mixture until smooth. Next, add the spinach, onion, cheese and pepper then mix.

Heat a non-stick pan over a medium to low heat. Add the remaining teaspoon of oil and wipe it around the pan with kitchen paper, before adding ¼ of the mixture. Spread it around the pan with the back of a spoon, about 12-15cm diameter and ½cm thick.
Cook for 2-3 minutes, then flip over with a spatula and cook for another minute or two on the other side.Serve topped with fresh tomatoes sprinkled with basil and black pepper.
hints: Try adding other vegetables to the pancakes such as grated courgette, cooked leeks or mushrooms.
Keep the pancakes warm between two plates, over a saucepan of gently simmering water, until they are all cooked.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 1

title: Black eyed bean, feta and herb burgers
description: A tasty meat-free burger packed with protein.
ingredients: 400g tin black-eyed beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Heat half the oil in a non-stick frying pan and fry the spring onions for 1–2 minutes, until softened.
Place the black-eyed beans in a large bowl and roughly mash. Stir in the remaining ingredients and combine well.
Divide the mixture into 6 and form each into patties or burgers.

Place on a baking sheet, brush each side with the remaining oil and chill for at least 30 minutes, or until required. Cook for 2–3 minutes on each side on a medium barbecue or grill until cooked through.
Serve in a wholemeal roll and fill with green salad, tomatoes and red onion.
hints: The nutritional analysis above includes a wholemeal bun as a serving suggestion.
You could use other beans such as kidney beans, cannelini or mixed beans.
Add crushed garlic and chilli flakes for extra flavour.
Cut the carbs, by enjoying this veggie burger without the bun.
Freezing instructions: Freeze in individually wrapped portions with grease proof paper between each burger. Defrost thoroughly and reheat until piping hot throughout.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 0

title: Roast butternut squash and red lentil soup
description: A warm, hearty soup that's easy to make, low in fat, high in fibre and satisfyingly filling.
ingredients: 1 litre reduced salt vegetable stock cube
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C/gas 7. Cut the butternut squash into quarters lengthways, scoop out the seeds, brush with a little of the oil and bake in the oven for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile, add the onion and carrot to the pan with 1 tsp of the oil, cook gently for a few minutes, until the onion starts to brown.
Now, pour the stock into the pan and add the lentils, stir together and simmer for around 15 minutes.
Remove the butternut squash from the oven, scoop out the flesh and add to the soup.
Simmer for a further 5 minutes, add a good pinch of pepper, then whizz with a stick blender or in a food processor until smooth.
Serve with a swirl of half-fat crème fraiche and a few chopped chives.
hints: This recipe is high in vitamin A, which helps your immune system function at its best.

Stock cubes contain salt, so don't add any extra salt during cooking. When simmering the soup, you'll be reducing the water content and concentrating the salt content, so taste it once cooked and add salt only if needed.
Freezing instructions: Freeze in portions then defrost in the fridge, or defrost in a microwave and reheat thoroughly until piping-hot.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 3

title: Red lentil soup
description: A tasty soup that's both warming and nutritious.
steps: Place the lentils, onion, carrot, garlic and stock into a pan, bring to the boil and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Transfer to a blender with the crème fraîche and parsley and blend until smooth. Season and serve with a chunk of bread
hints: For a vegan version, simply omit the crème fraîche or add 4 tbsp soya milk instead.
Spice it up with 1 tsp curry paste or powder or a pinch of chilli flakes.
Freezing instructions: Freeze in portions then defrost in the fridge, or defrost in a microwave, taking care to stir regularly.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 2

title: Microwave mug: Apple and cinnamon fruity porridge
description: This fruity porridge is warming, filling and quick to make – ideal for a healthy start.
ingredients: 1 tsp cinnamon, plus pinch to top
steps: Add the oats, optional sweetener, cinnamon and apple to a mug and mix.
Add 100ml water and cook at full power (800W) for two minutes.
Add the milk, mix and sprinkle over a little cinnamon.
hints: You could use pear or banana instead of apple or add a little dried fruit, such as prunes or raisins.
Try adding a few chopped nuts, or sunflower or pumpkin seeds.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 1

title: Chilli con carne
description: This warming chilli is a hearty classic which always goes down well. Packed with veg and protein, it's a quick and easy go-to meal.
ingredients: 1–2 tsp chilli powder (hot or mild as you prefer)
steps: Add the oil to a large pan, then add the onions and cook for 3–4 minutes until just starting to brown.
Add the minced beef and cook for 5–7 minutes (or until cooked thoroughly), breaking up any clumps with a wooden spoon.
Add the mushrooms, peppers, courgette and garlic. Cook for a further 7–8 minutes, stirring regularly until they soften.
Stir in the chilli, oregano, cumin and tomatoes, then cover with a lid and simmer gently for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the lentils and beans, and mix well. Cover and simmer for a further 5 minutes.
Stir in the chocolate until melted. Serve with salad.
hints: Dark chocolate intensifies the flavours and is healthier and works better than other types of chocolate.
Freezing instructions: Suitable for freezing once cooked. Defrost fully in the fridge and reheat until piping hot throughout, stirring regularly.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 3

title: Apple and cranberry sauce
description: A quick and easy sauce to accompany your Christmas dinner.
steps: Core and roughly chop the apples, then add them to a pan with a dash of water. Add the cranberry sauce and dried cranberries.
Gently heat through, stirring regularly for 5–6 minutes until the apples have softened.
hints: Store in the fridge.
Freezing instructions: Suitable for freezing once cooked. Freeze in portions then defrost and serve cold or warm.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 0

title: Barbecued fruit
description: An interesting twist on barbecued food, using fruit instead of savoury items.
ingredients: 5 slices of honeydew melon, cut into cubes (edible flesh 500g)
steps: Simply mix together all the ingredients, divide between 6 large squares of foil and secure into parcels.
Cook over the barbeque coals for about 10–12 minutes and serve.
hints: Why not try a tropical version - use mangoes and pineapple.
Works well with different spices, such as cinnamon or ground ginger.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 2

title: Baked eggs with spinach, mushroom and chips
description: This tasty baked egg dish is a perfect vegetarian option for lunch or dinner. The homemade chips on the side are great for dipping in those egg yolks. This recipe was selected in partnership with Slimming World.
ingredients: 750g floury potatoes, such as Maris Piper or King Edward, cut into chips
600g frozen spinach, defrosted and well squeezed out
steps: Preheat your oven to 200°C/ fan 180°C/gas 6. Spread the chips on a large, non-stick baking tray in a single layer. Spray with a couple of pumps of low calorie cooking spray and season with pepper. Bake for 40 minutes, or until golden, turning halfway.

Meanwhile, spray a large, non-stick frying pan with a couple of pumps of low-calorie cooking spray and place over a medium-high heat. Once hot, add the onion and mushrooms, and stir-fry for 5-6 minutes until softened and a little coloured. Stir in the nutmeg and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant, then add the spinach and stir everything together until piping hot throughout. Remove from the heat and stir through the yoghurt, then season with pepper.

Either divide the mixture between 4 individual pie dishes, or tip into 1 large pie dish. Make 4 wells in the mixture and crack an egg into each. Top with a twist of black pepper and bake on the shelf below the chips for the remaining 15 minutes of the chips’ cooking time, or until the egg whites have set. Divide the chips between 4 plates and serve with the baked eggs.
hints: You can use a plain yoghurt of your choice. However, this will change the nutritional information and texture of the dish.

At risk groups such as infants, children, pregnant women, the elderly and those who are unwell should avoid soft/lightly cooked and raw eggs, unless they can guarantee that they are produced under the Lion code quality assurance scheme.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 3

title: Wholemeal fruit bars
description: Ideal for lunch boxes or for a healthy snack.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180ºC/gas 4 and lightly grease a 19cm x 28cm baking tray.
Place the raisins, sugar, spread and mixed spice into a medium pan with 200ml of water.
Bring to the boil, then remove from the heat and cool.
In a separate dish, stir together the remaining ingredients then stir into the raisin mixture. Spoon into the prepared tin, smooth out to 1½ cm thick then bake for 25–30 minutes.
Immediately after removing from the oven mark into 25 bars.
Allow to cool, and serve.
hints: Try adding different spices such as cinnamon or ground ginger.
You can also use dried fruits such a mixed dried fruit, sultanas, prunes or apricots.
Freezing instructions: Suitable for freezing once cooked. Freeze in portions then defrost and serve cold or warm.

title: Turkish cauliflower pizza with Quorn and tzatziki
description: Cauliflower makes a healthy and lower-carb alternative to a traditional pizza base.
ingredients: For the base: 900 g/32 oz cauliflower, prepared into florets
40g/3 oz 3% fat cream cheese, e. g. Philadelphia lightest cream cheese or 40g/3 oz low fat natural yoghurt
For the toppings: 1 tsp olive oil
1 large cucumber, half grated, half finely diced
steps: For the base: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180° fan)/400F/gas mark 6. Grease and line a large round baking tray with greaseproof paper.
Place the cauliflower florets in a food processor and pulse until rice-like in texture. Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil and cook the cauliflower, covered, for 4-5 minutes until tender.

Drain well and gather the cauliflower in a large square of muslin or cheesecloth. You can also use a clean tea towel. Wrap the muslin around the cauliflower in a ball-shape and twist well to wring out as much excess water as possible.
Tip the dried cauliflower into a bowl and add the egg, cream cheese, flour, and freshly ground black pepper. Mix well until a rough dough comes together.
Transfer the cauliflower dough onto the lined tray and roll out into a large round. Brush the top with olive oil.
Bake for 25-35 minutes until dry to the touch and golden-brown all over.
For the toppings: In the meantime, heat the olive oil in a sauté pan set over a medium heat until hot.
Add the onion and sweat until softened, about 5 minutes. Stir in the Quorn and cook over a slightly increased heat until browned all over, breaking it up with a wooden spoon.
Stir in the spices and oregano, cooking for a further 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and cover to keep warm.
Remove the cauliflower base from the oven when ready. Top with the Quorn, diced cucumber, cherry tomatoes, and chopped parsley.
Stir the grated cucumber into the yoghurt in a small mixing bowl. Spoon dollops on top of the pizza and serve the remainder on the side.
hints: Replace the Quorn mince in this recipe with slices of grilled pepper or aubergine to increase your veg intake.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 4

title: Chickpea and tuna salad
description: Filling chunks of tuna with chickpeas, make this dish ideal for lunch on the go.
ingredients: 180g ripe cherry tomatoes, cut into quarters
1 x 400g tin chickpeas in water, drained (drained weight 240g)
1 x 200g tin tuna in water, drained (drained weight 150g)
steps: Add the lemon zest to a large bowl with the pepper, and olive oil.
Next, add the red onion, tomatoes and cucumber, mix well and leave to infuse for a couple of minutes.
Add the chickpeas and tuna, and fold in gently so everything is coated with the dressing.
Finally, toss in the salad leaves and divide between two lunch boxes, packed with a lemon wedge to squeeze over before eating.
hints: Acidic ingredients, like lemon juice, will make your salad go limp, so take a wedge of lemon in your packed lunch to use just before eating.
Salmon or prawns make a good alternative to tuna. For a vegan version, try pieces of marinated tofu.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 4

title: Mushroom ragu
description: A rich mushroom ragu which goes excellently with spiralised veg.
steps: Put the oil in a pan and gently cook the leek for 3–4 minutes, stirring regularly.
Add the mushrooms, garlic, chilli and oregano. Continue cooking gently for 5 minutes, still stirring regularly. Meanwhile, toast the seeds and reserve.
Plunge the spiralised vegetables (homemade or ready prepared) into boiling water for 2 minutes.
Just before serving, stir the yoghurt into the mushrooms.
Divide the spiralised vegetables between 2 bowls. Top each with the mushroom sauce, and sprinkle with toasted seeds, black pepper, a few shavings of parmesan and a sprig of basil.
hints: Other spiralised vegetables work well with this dish, such as butternut squash or beetroot.
For a higher-carb option, serve with wholegrain pasta instead of spiralised veg.
For a vegetarian alternative to Parmesan, swap it out with vegetarian-style hard cheese.
You can use an unsweetened plain yoghurt of your choice, but this will change the nutrition information and texture of the dish.
Fruit/veg portions
Fruit/veg portions per serving: 4
